αἰνῇ: αἰνός — dread, grim, terrible; fem. dat. sg., Ionic -ῃ (= Attic -ᾷ)
αἶσαν: αἶσα — portion, share, lot; fem. acc. sg. (ἀπὸ ληίδος αἶσαν ’his share of the spoil’)
βάλλετε: βάλλω — throw, cast, put; pres. imper. 2 pl.: ’throw on, spread’
βίη: βίη — might, bodily strength, force; fem. nom. sg.
βουλοίμην: βούλομαι — wish, prefer; pres. opt. 1 sg.: ‘I would wish’
γνοίης: γιγνώσκω — come to know, recognise; aor. opt. 2 sg., potential after κε: ’you would come to know’
γυναῖκά: γυνή — woman, wife; fem. acc. sg.
δήμῳ: δῆμος — district, land, people; dat. sg.
δείσας: δείδω — fear, be afraid; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having grown afraid’
δηϊοτῆτι: δηϊοτής — fighting, battle; fem. dat. sg., epic (δήϊος ’hostile’)
δουρὸς: δόρυ — spear, wood; neut. gen. sg., epic (= Attic δόρατος)
δοῦρε: δόρυ — spear, shaft; acc. dual, epic stem δουρ-: ’two spears’
εἶσιν: εἶμι — go; pres. 3 sg., with future sense: ’will go’ (= Attic εἶσι(ν))
εἷλε: αἱρέω — take, take away; aor. 3 sg. act., augmented: ’took’
θεοειδέα: θεοειδής — godlike, of godlike form; masc. acc. sg., uncontracted (= Attic θεοειδῆ)
θεοειδής: θεοειδής — godlike in form (θεός + εἶδος); masc. nom. sg.
κέρδιον: κερδίων — more profitable, better; neut. nom. sg., comparative of κέρδος
καμπύλα: καμπύλος — curved, bent; neut. acc. pl.
κατέχευεν: καταχέω — pour down over; aor. 3 sg.
κεκορυθμένα: κορύσσω — arm, equip with a helmet or point; perf. mid./pass. part. neut. acc. pl.: ’armed’ (with bronze)
κονίῃσι: κονία — dust; fem. dat. pl., epic -ῃσι (= Attic κονίαις)
κραδίη: κραδίη — heart; fem. nom. sg. · also fem. voc. sg. (same form): ’heart!’ (τέτλαθι δή, κραδίη ’endure now, heart’)
κτήμαθ: κτῆμα — possession, piece of property; neut. nom./acc. pl., elided (κτήματα)
κτήμασι: κτῆμα — possession, property; neut. dat. pl.
κύνες: κύων — dog; masc. nom. pl. · also masc. voc. pl., in address: ’dogs!’ (ὦ κύνες)
λάϊνον: λάϊνος — of stone, stone; masc. acc. sg., epic (= Attic λίθινος)
λώβην: λώβη — outrage, insult, abuse; fem. acc. sg.
μέσσον: μέσος — middle, in the middle; neut. acc. sg., epic -σσ- (= Attic μέσον), used as a noun: ’the middle’ · also adverbial neut. acc. sg.: ’midway’ (μέσσον ὑπὲρ Κρήτης ’midway over Crete’) · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with αὐχένα: ’in the middle’ (κατ’ αὐχένα μέσσον ’in the middle of the neck’)
μέσσῳ: μέσος — middle, in the middle; masc. dat. sg., epic doubled-σ (= Attic μέσῳ): ’in the midst of’
μενέλαον: Μενέλαος — Menelaus, king of Sparta, brother of Agamemnon; acc. sg.
νείκεσσεν: νεικέω — quarrel with, revile; aor. 3 sg., epic -σσ-, unaugmented, ν-movable
νικήσῃ: νικάω — win, conquer; aor. subj. 3 sg., after κε/αἴ κεν: ’shall win’
πέλει: πέλω — be, come to be, exist; pres. 3 sg. (= Attic ἐστί): ’there is’
παράκοιτιν: παράκοιτις — wife, bedfellow; fem. acc. sg.
πατρί: πατήρ — father; masc. dat. sg. · also masc. dat. sg. after ἐπιπείθομαι, ’obey’: ’(obeyed his) father’ (φίλῳ ἐπεπείθετο πατρί)
προκαλίζετο: προκαλίζομαι — challenge, call out (+ inf.); impf. 3 sg. mid.
προμάχοισι: πρόμαχος — front-fighter, champion; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
προπάροιθεν: προπάροιθεν — before, in front, in one’s presence; adv.
πῆμα: πῆμα — woe, calamity, disaster; neut. nom. sg. · also neut. acc. sg., direct object: ’woe’
σιγῇ: σιγή — silence; fem. dat. sg. used adverbially: ’in silence’
στεῦται: στεῦμαι — stand forth as promising, declare, claim (defective); 3 sg. στεῦται, + inf.: ’he declares’
σχεδὸν: σχεδόν — near, close by (+ gen.); adv. · also + dat.: σχεδὸν ἀλλήλῃσι ’close to one another’
σῷ: σός — your, yours; masc./neut. dat. sg.
τέχνῃ: τέχνη — skill, craft, art; fem. dat. sg., dative of means
τίσεσθαι: τίνω (mid. τίνυμαι) — pay; mid. take vengeance; fut. inf. mid., in indirect statement after φῆ: ’to take vengeance’
ταί: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. nom. pl., epic (= Attic αἱ): ’they’ · also relative, fem. nom. pl.: ’which’ (ταί τ’ ἀμβροσίην … φέρουσιν ’which bear ambrosia’)
ταχέες: ταχύς — swift, fast; masc. nom. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic ταχεῖς)
τεύχεσιν: τεῦχος — armour, gear; neut. dat. pl., ν-movable
τιτυσκόμενοι: τιτύσκομαι — aim at, take aim; pres. part. mid. masc. nom. pl.
τοιόσδε: τοιόσδε, -ήδε, -όνδε — such (as this); masc. nom. sg.
τρόμος: τρόμος — trembling, quaking; masc. nom. sg.
τόξα: τόξον — bow; neut. nom./acc. pl. (plural for a single bow)
φιλότητα: φιλότης — friendship, love, kindness; fem. acc. sg.
φωτὸς: φώς — man, mortal; masc. gen. sg.
φύγον: φεύγω — flee, escape; aor. 3 pl., no augment (= ἔφυγον) · also aor. 1 sg. (same ending as 3 pl.): ’I fled’
χ: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν); elided and aspirated χ’ before a rough breathing
χάρμα: χάρμα — joy, delight; neut. nom. sg.
χαμᾶζε: χαμᾶζε — to the ground, down to earth; adv. (χαμαί + -δε)
χρυσέης: χρύσεος — golden; fem. gen. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic χρυσῆς)
ἀθέσφατον: ἀθέσφατος — immense, prodigious (sense of the word debated); adj., fem. acc. sg., agreeing with θάλασσαν
ἀκούσας: ἀκούω — hear (+ gen. of person/thing heard); aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having heard, on hearing’
ἀλεείνων: ἀλεείνω — shun, avoid; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.
ἀλκή: ἀλκή — defence, strength to resist; fem. nom. sg.
ἀλλοδαποῖσι: ἀλλοδαπός — of another land, foreign; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις), used substantively: ’to men of other lands’
ἀμείνω: ἀμείνων — better (comparative of ἀγαθός); neut. nom. pl., contracted from ἀμείνονα
ἀνέρος: ἀνήρ — man; masc. gen. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic ἀνδρός)
ἀρίστους: ἀγαθός — good; superlative ἄριστος, masc. acc. pl.: ’best’
ἀρηΐφιλος: ἀρηΐφιλος — dear to Ares, war-loving; adj. (2-term.), masc. nom. sg., epithet of Menelaus
ἄγριον: ἄγριος — wild, savage; masc. acc. sg. · also neut. nom. sg., predicate, ’savage’ (of the monster, with κακόν)
ἐνόησεν: νοέω — perceive, devise, think of; aor. 3 sg.
ἐρέειν: ἐρέω (= εἴρω/λέγω) — say, tell, speak; fut. inf., epic uncontracted -έειν (= Attic ἐρεῖν)
ἐρίηρας: ἐρίηρος — traditionally ’trusty’, exact sense uncertain (of companions); masc. acc. pl.
ἐρικυδέα: ἐρικυδής — very glorious, splendid; fem. acc. sg., epic uncontracted
ἐρχόμενον: ἔρχομαι — go, come; pres. part. masc. acc. sg.: ’as he went’
ἐχάρη: χαίρω — rejoice, be glad; aor. 3 sg., passive form with active sense: ’rejoiced’
ἑκὼν: ἑκών — willing, of one’s own accord; masc. nom. sg.
ἑλένῃ: Ἑλένη — Helen, wife of Menelaus; fem. dat. sg.
ἑτάρους: ἕταρος — companion (by-form of ἑταῖρος); acc. pl.
ἔδυ: δύω — go in, sink, set (of the sun); aor. 3 sg. (root aorist)
ἔλλαβε: λαμβάνω — take, win, get; aor. 3 sg., augmented with double λ, epic (= Attic ἔλαβε)
ἔμεναι: εἰμί — be; pres. inf., epic (= Attic εἶναι)
ἔριδα: ἔρις — strife, rivalry, contest; fem. acc. sg.
ἕλοιτο: αἱρέω — take, get for oneself; aor. opt. mid. 3 sg., purpose after a past tense: ’that he might take’ · also in an alternative deliberation (ἠὲ … ἦ …): ’should take’ (ἠὲ … ἐκ θυμὸν ἕλοιτο ’whether he should take his life out’)
ἕσσο: ἕννυμι — clothe; mid./pass. be clothed, wear; plpf. mid./pass. 2 sg., epic: ’you were clothed in’
ἰδών: ὁράω (aor. εἶδον) — see; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having seen’
ἰόντες: εἶμι — go, come; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ‘coming’ · also ’going’ rather than ’coming’, the precise direction supplied by context: Τροίηθεν ἰόντες ’setting out from Troy, departing’
ἱππόβοτον: ἱππόβοτος — horse-feeding, horse-pasturing; neut. acc. sg., epithet of Argos
ἴσχεσθ: ἴσχω — hold; mid. hold oneself back, stop; pres. imper. 2 pl. mid., elided (ἴσχεσθ’ = ἴσχεσθε)
ἵησιν: ἵημι — send, throw; pres. 3 sg. (Attic ἵησι): ’sends, throws’
ὀφέλλει: ὀφέλλω — owe, be liable for; pres. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ὀφείλει)
ὀχέων: ὀχέω — bear, carry; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’bearing’
ὁππότερος: ὁππότερος — whichever of the two; masc. nom. sg., indefinite relative (= Attic ὁπότερος)
ὅμιλον: ὅμιλος — crowd, throng; masc. acc. sg.
ὅσον: ὅσος — as much as, as many as; masc. acc. sg. or neut. nom./acc. sg.; neut. often adverbial: ’as much as’
ὅσσα: ὅσος — as much/many as; epic ὅσσος (double σ), neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’as many as’
ὑπό: ὑπό — under, beneath; prep. + dat., accented ὑπό before the enclitic σοι
ὠκεανοῖο: Ὠκεανός — Ocean, the river encircling the earth; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -οῦ)
ῥοάων: ῥοή — stream, flow; fem. gen. pl., epic -άων (= Attic -ῶν)
